bull.b: Oracle's subscription-heavy cloud, support, and application revenue is tied to ongoing customer use and renewals. That recurring base can smooth revenue, deepen account relationships, and provide funding and cross-selling capacity as customers migrate workloads to OCI.

Cloud infrastructure growth of 93% and RPO of $638B show accelerating demand plus unusually strong multi-year revenue visibility. The mix of AI workloads, database services, and contracted commitments can support sustained expansion as capacity comes online over the next several quarters.

Operating cash flow reached $32B and rose 54% year over year, demonstrating that Oracle's core operations are generating substantial cash. That cash generation provides an internal funding base for infrastructure expansion, even though heavy investment currently reduces free cash flow.

bear.b: Debt increased from about $75.9B in 2022 to $156.2B in 2026, while debt-to-equity remained about 3.6x. This debt-heavy structure raises financing sensitivity and reduces flexibility if infrastructure spending, growth timing, or cash conversion underperform.

Oracle expects roughly $70B of FY2027 net CapEx cash outlay, while recent free cash flow turned deeply negative. The scale of spending can intensify reliance on external financing and make earnings quality and liquidity more dependent on timely data-center utilization and customer payments.

Gross margin already stepped down around five percentage points and is expected to decline further in FY2027 as new data centers ramp. Until sites reach full contractual revenue and utilization, faster infrastructure growth may dilute consolidated profitability and constrain earnings conversion.
